result.title: Accuracy Is Not Value: Choosing Weak Supervisors by What the Student Inherits
result.summary: Weak supervisors are usually judged by their own errors, but what matters is what a student learns from them. For squared loss and any linear learner shared by all supervisors, we show that a supervisor's value is determined by its errors after they pass through the student's learning operator. Consequently, the inner products of the supervisors' raw errors can be compatible with every feasible value of the student's risk, and weighting supervisors by them can be arbitrarily worse than the best weighting in relative excess risk. This student-relative value is not identifiable from unlabeled data, but what is missing is small: one finite-dimensional projection of the target decides whether training on a weak aggregate helps, another decides how to weight the supervisors. Known teacher training rules, or a label-model condition stated in student-relative form, shrink it further. Clean labels close the remaining gap at a cost set by the geometry of the unresolved directions rather than by the dimension of the student's representation, with matching worst-case lower bounds. In Gaussian designs we also quantify when exact teacher structure beats ordinary stacking and when weak supervisors, combined with clean labels, beat every procedure that uses the clean labels alone. The guarantees extend to fitted ridge students and finite unlabeled data.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究弱监督者的价值应如何评估，证明在平方损失与共享线性学习器下，监督者价值取决于其误差经学生学习算子过滤后的形态，并分析用未标注数据和少量干净标签恢复该学生相对价值的加权与风险界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「监督价值须相对学生而非监督者自身误差衡量」的视角，可供核查 LVR 中多条推理轨迹或弱监督信号的加权与贡献分配问题；但结论限于线性学习和平方损失的理论设定，迁移到 latent 监督前需验证适用性。
